intended_object: The unique (empty) simple function on an empty measurable space α, with values in any type β. This comes from the docstring "Simple function defined on the empty type."
explanation: When α is empty there is exactly one function α → β, the empty function `isEmptyElim`. It is trivially a simple function: its range is empty, hence finite, and every preimage is the empty set, hence measurable. The definition builds it with `ofFinite`. That function turns any function on a finite type with a measurable space structure into a simple function, and an empty type counts as finite through the instance derived from `IsEmpty`. The definition puts no conditions on β and only needs a `MeasurableSpace` on α, which is already the most general setting. It is the trivial degenerate case of a simple function. It is a real mathematical object, if a trivial one, so I did not class it as a technical device. A search of Mathlib/MeasureTheory found no use of `ofIsEmpty` outside its own definition. The definition matches its docstring.
